Disparate

/DIS-puh-rit/ · adjective

Hear It

No recording available for this word.

What It Means

Disparate means fundamentally different, or made up of sharply contrasting and unrelated parts

Disparate means fundamentally different, or made up of sharply contrasting and unrelated parts. The planning committee united people with disparate backgrounds, from dairy farmers to software engineers.

Worked Example

Dev's road-trip playlist jumps from opera to country to electronic dance music. His friends tease him that the songs are so disparate that no two of them sound like they belong on the same playlist.

The songs are not just slightly different; they come from sharply contrasting, unrelated genres, which is the extreme kind of difference disparate describes.

How Disparate Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

dissimilar

dissimilar: not alike in character or quality

contrasting

contrasting: strikingly different when compared

unrelated

unrelated: having no connection to one another

Antonyms

similar

similar: alike in significant ways

matching

matching: corresponding or going together

How Strong Is It? — different → irreconcilable → disparate

different vs. disparate

different vs. disparate: Different can describe any two things that are not the same, while disparate suggests elements so unlike that they barely seem to belong together.

irreconcilable vs. disparate

irreconcilable vs. disparate: Disparate is milder than irreconcilable, which means so deeply opposed that the elements can never be brought into agreement.

Build the Word

The pieces

Prefix — dis-

Prefix — dis-: apart, not the same

Root — par

Root — par: equal (Latin par)

Suffix — -ate

Suffix — -ate: having the quality of (adjective-forming)

Put it together

Put it together: This word genuinely fits the unit's 'not, opposite of' pattern: dis- (apart, not the same) plus Latin par (equal) gives 'not equal, not matching,' which is exactly what disparate things are.

Use the root in a new word: parity

Use the root in a new word: parity: By June the two teams had reached parity in the standings, with exactly equal records.

Word Choice

Formal, academic

Disparate is stronger than merely different: it signals that the elements are so unlike that they barely seem to belong together. It appears constantly in academic and journalistic writing about combining disparate sources, fields, communities, or data sets.
